headline: Gusty winds and a chilly Friday follow today's storm, with light snow and a bit of freezing drizzle near the Tennessee border tonight, then a quick warm-up and a fast shot of rain on Sunday evening.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Around Charlotte, low clouds, patchy fog and occasional light rain hang on through the afternoon, then gusty southwest winds take over by late afternoon and help clear out the fog. Gusts of 25 to 35 mph peak this evening into the early overnight, with occasional gusts near 40 mph in parts of the North Carolina Piedmont and the high mountains, enough to blow around loose objects and cause scattered power outages, though just short of Wind Advisory levels. In the mountains, rain or snow becomes likely this evening as colder air arrives, with 1 to 2 inches of snow mostly on the higher peaks of western Graham and Macon Counties and possible slick high-elevation roads; light freezing rain or drizzle is also possible overnight in the North Carolina counties along the Tennessee border, even in the valleys.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday stays breezy, with winds slowly easing through the day, and it will be chilly under lingering clouds, with highs about 10 degrees below normal and lows Friday night about 5 degrees below normal. Saturday turns dry, and temperatures climb quickly into the weekend ahead of the next cold front. That fast-moving front brings more gusty winds and rain to everyone Sunday evening, with about 0.1 to 0.33 inch in the eastern half of the area, including the Charlotte region, and 0.25 to 0.5 inch in the western half; brief snow showers are possible on the highest peaks along the Tennessee–North Carolina border late Sunday night.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Monday through Thursday look dry across the region. Temperatures should stay close to normal, mostly within 2 to 3 degrees of average, after the Sunday front passes.

watch_for: Strong gusts near 40 mph this evening in the NC Piedmont and mountains, with possible scattered power outages
Slick high-elevation roads and possible light freezing drizzle near the Tennessee border tonight into Friday
Timing of Sunday evening's fast-moving rain and gusty winds
confidence: Forecasters are fairly confident in the gusty winds and light mountain snow tonight and in rain for everyone Sunday evening, with dry, near-normal weather expected next week.
